questions.text: "___ terms of communicative effectiveness, intelligibility matters more than accent."
questions.hint: "In terms of" = regarding, with respect to

questions.text: "___ ___ to language policy, there are no easy answers in multilingual societies."
questions.hint: "With regard to" = concerning

questions.text: "___ the perspective of World Englishes research, no variety is inherently superior."
questions.hint: "From the perspective of" = as seen through a specific lens

questions.text: "___ far ___ language learners ___ concerned, communicative effectiveness is the key goal."
questions.hint: "As far as [plural] are concerned" = when it comes to

questions.text: "___ the context of ELF, the native speaker norm is not the primary reference point."
questions.hint: "In the context of" = within the domain of

questions.text: "___ ___ the evidence, a fundamental rethinking of language teaching is needed." (considering the evidence)
questions.correct: In view of / In light of
questions.hint: "In view of / In light of + noun" = given, considering

questions.text: "___ ___ their multilingual experience, these speakers communicate more flexibly." (because of)
questions.hint: "By virtue of + noun" = because of

questions.text: "The curriculum was redesigned ___ ___ ___ ___ promoting intercultural competence." (with the aim of)
questions.hint: "With a view to + gerund"

questions.text: "___ ___ equity, all accents and varieties should receive equal respect."
questions.hint: "In the interests of + noun" = for the benefit of

questions.text: "The model is useful ___ ___ ___ it accounts for communicative context." (to the degree that)
questions.hint: "To the extent that + clause" = qualifying phrase

questions.text: Why did English spread globally?
opts: Because it is intrinsically superior to other languages
Through British colonialism and US dominance — not linguistic superiority
Because it has the simplest grammar
questions.correct: Through British colonialism and US dominance — not linguistic superiority
questions.hint: Reading 1: "through the mechanisms of British colonialism… US dominance"

questions.text: "___ ___ of this study, ELF is defined as English used between non-native speakers."
questions.hint: "For the purposes of + noun/gerund" = for the reason of

questions.text: "Correction is appropriate only ___ ___ ___ the error genuinely impedes understanding." (to the degree that)
questions.hint: "To the extent that + clause"

questions.text: "With a view to ___ intercultural citizens, language teachers have a special responsibility." (gerund)
questions.hint: "With a view to + gerund" — not infinitive

questions.text: What does Dr. Pemberton say ELF communication prioritises?
opts: Conformity to American academic writing standards
Clarity, repair strategies, accommodation, and flexibility
questions.correct: Clarity, repair strategies, accommodation, and flexibility
questions.hint: Listening 3B: ELF norms

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ the above, it can be concluded that language policy has direct social consequences." (given)
questions.correct: In light of / In view of
questions.hint: "In light of the above" = formal conclusion phrase

questions.text: Which sentence contains an error?
opts: "In terms of its global reach, English is unrivalled."
"With regard to language policy, there are no easy answers."
"By virtue to their experience, they communicated well."
"From the perspective of ELF research, intelligibility matters most."
questions.correct: "By virtue to their experience, they communicated well."
questions.hint: "By virtue OF" — always "of" not "to"

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___, language education must evolve to reflect global communication realities." (given what has been argued)
questions.correct: In light of the above / In view of the above
questions.hint: "In light of/In view of the above" = given what has been discussed

questions.text: What is "English as a Lingua Franca" (ELF)?
opts: English as the official language of the EU
English used as a shared language between speakers who don't share a first language
A simplified form of English for global business
English as taught in British schools abroad
questions.correct: English used as a shared language between speakers who don't share a first language
questions.hint: Reading 1: "shared language between speakers who do not share a first language"

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ its colonial history, English carries cultural assumptions that learners should understand." (because of)
questions.hint: "By virtue of + noun" = because of, on account of

questions.text: "The distinction is analytically valuable ___ ___ it captures the key dimensions of cultural variation." (insofar as)
questions.hint: "Insofar as + clause" = to the degree that

questions.text: The practice of alternating between two or more languages within a single conversation is called ___.
questions.hint: Reading 2: code-switching

questions.text: "___ relation to intercultural competence, perspective-taking is the most fundamental skill."
questions.hint: "In relation to" = in connection with, concerning

questions.text: "With a view to improve" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "With a view to + GERUND": "with a view to improving" — not infinitive

questions.text: What is "linguistic imperialism"?
opts: A policy of banning minority languages
The idea that the spread of English involves imposing cultural values of dominant powers
The natural dominance of all major languages
A UN policy on language rights
questions.correct: The idea that the spread of English involves imposing cultural values of dominant powers
questions.hint: Reading 1: "linguistic imperialism"
